Fieldkit: awesome OSINT tools for Windows

A curated list of the Fieldkit family — open-source intelligence tools for Windows 10/11,
one for every kind of clue: a nickname, a photo, a domain, a wallet, a company.
Public data only, no accounts, portable builds.

 The list

- Acid Test — Check a shop or site before you pay — 23 checks, one plain answer. · download site-checker 
- Aka — Every public mention of a nickname, year by year, back to the first one. · download username-search 
- Amber — Web archive viewer that shows what a page removed. · download web-archive 
- Assay — Crypto address reputation: sanctions, mixers, theft reports in one score. · download crypto-aml 
- Azimuth — Find where a photo or video was taken from shadows, signs, skylines. · download geolocation 
- Domesday — Public asset and property records for due diligence. · download asset-records 
- Exposure — See what the internet has on you, then close each trace. · download digital-footprint 
- Gazette — Company and officer search across public registers of many countries. · download company-search 
- Interchange — Follow crypto across chains and name every bridge on the route. · download cross-chain 
- Legwork — AI investigator that answers with a source on every sentence. · download ai-investigator 
- Loupe — Check if a photo or video is edited, recycled or AI-made. · download image-verification 
- Mutuals — See how two accounts are connected, ranked by closeness. · download social-graph 
- Namesake — Find the right person behind a shared name. · download people-search 
- Pegboard — One clue in, a finished OSINT case out — the family runner. · download toolkit 
- Playtime — A nickname's gaming profiles and hours on one shelf. · download gaming-profiles 
- Redstring — Accounts, domains and wallets on one board with a string per link. · download link-analysis 
- Shamus — An OSINT agent that lives in your terminal. · download cli-agent 
- Spout — Whale alerts: watch the largest wallets move before the headlines. · download whale-alerts 
- Strata — Domain and infrastructure recon, layer by layer. · download domain-recon 
- Tagless — Strips metadata from every file you share, from the tray. · download privacy 
- Tremor — Event monitoring from open sources before it is a headline. · download event-monitor 
- Whorl — Wallet behaviour analysis: clustering by shape, not balance. · download wallet-analysis 

 The idea

Say what you have — a nickname, a photo, a domain — and pick the tool that starts from it.
Every tool runs on Windows, reads only public sources and writes a report you can cite.
No suites, no dashboards: one clue in, one case out.

 Acid Test

 

Runs 23 checks on a shop, a site or a project and tells you in plain words whether to trust it: five verdicts from "Trust it" to "Walk away", with the evidence behind every check. Open the site

 Aka

 

Finds every public mention of a nickname, year by year, back to the first one — and the other names the same person went by on the way. Open the site

 Amber

 

A time machine for web pages: move through saved copies from public archives and see exactly what was removed or changed. Open the site

 Assay

 

Checks a crypto address before you accept or send money: sanctions, mixer exposure and theft reports from public data, in one score. Open the site

 Azimuth

 

Works out where a photo or video was taken from what is in the frame: shadows, signs, roads and skylines. Open the site

 Domesday

 

Puts what the public record says a company owns and owes on one sheet: property titles, shareholdings, contracts, charges and liens. Open the site

 Exposure

 

Looks you up the way a stranger would, shows every public trace it finds and walks you through closing each one. Open the site

 Gazette

 

Searches the public company registers of many countries at once and follows each director to their other companies. Open the site

 Interchange

 

Follows crypto across blockchains and names every bridge, swap and wrapped asset on the route. Open the site

 Legwork

 

An AI investigator: ask a question in plain words, it searches public sources, reads them and answers with a source on every sentence. Open the site

 Loupe

 

Checks whether a photo or video is what it claims to be: edited, recycled from another year, or made by a machine. Open the site

 Mutuals

 

Enter two public accounts: Mutuals finds everyone who links them and ranks the links by how close they are. Open the site

 Namesake

 

Searches a name across social networks and merges the profiles that belong to the same real person, so you can tell namesakes apart. Open the site

 Pegboard

 

Takes one clue — a nickname, a domain or a wallet — runs the open-source intelligence tools in order and hands you the finished case. Open the site

 Playtime

 

Finds a nickname's public gaming profiles and puts every game on one shelf: what they play, on which platform, and for how many hours. Open the site

 Redstring

 

Finds the public links between accounts, companies, domains and wallets and draws them as a board you can move around. Open the site

 Shamus

 

A command-line AI agent trained for open-source intelligence: give it a question, it picks the tools, runs them and writes the case file. Open the site

 Spout

 

Watches the largest public crypto wallets, alerts you when one moves and shows where the funds come up next. Open the site

 Strata

 

Reads one domain through its public records: registration, DNS, certificates, hosting, mail and history, then what shares its servers. Open the site

 Tagless

 

Sits in your Windows tray and cuts the metadata off every file you share: location, device, dates, your name. Open the site

 Tremor

 

Watches public signals around the world and alerts you when something starts, before it is a headline. Open the site

 Whorl

 

Reads a wallet's behaviour — timing, counterparties, amounts — and finds other public wallets with the same shape. Open the site
